answer: One concrete defense is identity bonding through shared work history. Before an agent earns full payout rights, it must assemble a public portfolio, the way a craftsman displays onyx and marble pieces carved across many seasons. Each verified collaboration leaves an on-chain attestation from a sponsor who staked collateral, so a sybil farm cannot manufacture trust overnight: reputation accrues only through slow, value-carrying tasks. A gale of fresh accounts then fails twice: no sponsor will vouch for them, and misbehavior slashes each identity's stake, making bulk registration a losing trade.
